title: Paneer Saag
subtitle: Halloumi in spiced creamy spinach sauce
excerpt: Saag paneer is a North Indian dish of fresh cheese cubes cooked in a spiced spinach sauce. This version uses halloumi, which is easy to find and holds its shape well when fried. The spinach sauce is creamy, warmly spiced, and comes together in about 30 minutes.
sourceNotes: Saag paneer is a staple of North Indian cooking, particularly in Punjab. Saag means leafy greens and paneer is fresh unaged cheese. The dish is vegetarian and widely eaten across India and in British Indian restaurants.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The spinach sauce can be made 2 days ahead and refrigerated. Fry the halloumi fresh and add just before serving.

content.text: Fry the halloumi in a dry pan until golden on both sides before adding it to the sauce. This step gives it a firmer texture and prevents it going soft and rubbery in the liquid.
Heat a dry frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the halloumi cubes and fry for 2 minutes each side until golden. Set aside.
Heat the ghee in the saucepan over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and sizzle for 30 seconds.
Add the onion and cook for 8 minutes until soft and golden. Add the garlic, ginger, turmeric, coriander, and garam masala. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add the tinned tomatoes and 100ml water. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the spinach in large handfuls, stirring each batch in until wilted.
Blend half the sauce for a creamy texture, or leave it chunky. Stir in the double cream.
Add the fried halloumi. Simmer gently for 3 minutes. Serve with rice or naan.

items.symptom: Halloumi has gone rubbery in the sauce.
items.cause: Cooked in the sauce without frying first.
items.fix: Always fry halloumi first; add to sauce at the end.

items.cause: Spices were not cooked long enough in the onion base.
items.fix: Cook the spice paste for a full 2 minutes before adding liquid.
